messages.text: I'm already on SNAP. Is there anything else I might be eligible for? I'm pregnant.

Congratulations! Since you're already getting food assistance (SNAP), you may qualify for WIC and TennCare or CoverKids too. I need a few details to check.

1. How many people live with you and share food? What are their ages?
2. How many babies are you expecting? Does anyone in the home have a disability?

After that I'll ask about income before taxes.
Just me, I live alone. I'm expecting one baby. Nobody in the home has a disability.

Thanks. I need three more things to check WIC and TennCare:

1. How old are you?
2. What is your income before taxes, and how often are you paid (weekly, every two weeks, or monthly)? If you have no income, just say so.
3. Do you get other income, like unemployment, Social Security, or child support?
I'm 22. I make $1,400 a month before taxes, paid monthly. I don't get any other income, like unemployment, Social Security, or child support.

You'll probably qualify for both WIC and TennCare. Both came back as **likely**, which is a screening result and not a decision.

**WIC (food help for pregnant women, babies, and young children): likely**
- WIC serves pregnant women. Because you already get food assistance (SNAP), you automatically meet WIC's income test. ([7 CFR 246.7](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-246.7) and [7 CFR 246.2](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-246.2))
- You'll also have a short health and nutrition check at the clinic.
- **To apply:** Go to a local health department clinic, or call 1-800-DIAL-WIC (1-800-342-5942). The website is the [Tennessee Department of Health WIC page](https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html).

**TennCare (health coverage): likely**
- Pregnant women can get TennCare with income up to 250% of the poverty level. For you, counting yourself and your baby as 2 people, that limit is $4,509 a month. Your income of $1,400 a month is well under it. ([TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html) and [42 CFR 435.603](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/section-435.603))
- If you're approved, your baby is covered for the first year after birth. ([TennCare guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html))
- **To apply:** Use [TennCare Connect](https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/), or call 855-259-0701.

For free local help with applying, dial **211**.

Only the state agency decides who gets these programs. Applying is free, and you can apply even if a screening says it's unlikely.

Once your baby is born, tell your SNAP office. Your household size will change, and that can change your benefit.
